devops-bot: Alert: spike in TLS handshake failures observed in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 starting ~2024-02-14T02:12Z. metric: gateway.tls.handshake_fail_rate = 4.8% :rotating_light:
Maria: seeing same on prod-gateway and inference-edge, latency spikes too. clients report 502/handshake-failure.
Sam: any recent rotator runs or KMS changes?
Devon: rotator ran last night 02:00 UTC to replace intermediates. Keystore logs show repeated unwrap errors in eu region around the same time.
Devon: paste logs: 
```
2024-02-14T02:01:47Z keystore[rotator]: INFO starting rotation (intermediate->promote)
2024-02-14T02:01:52Z keystore[rotator]: ERROR kms:Decrypt failed for key alias/rotator-eu: AccessDenied
2024-02-14T02:02:01Z proxy[gateway-eu]: WARN tls: handshake failed: cipher_suite_lookup: unsupported key exchange
```
Kevin: AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt — that would make the rotator push an incomplete cert chain (missing private unwrap), clients then fail validation. But AccessDenied during unwrap should be transient; curious why proxy gets unsupported key exchange.
Frank: Could be session-ticket or ticket-encryption key mismatch too. If the server rotated the ticket encryption key but couldn't unwrap the new ticket key, resumes fail and some clients fallback to full handshake which then hits cert chain issues.
Maria: quick mitigation: roll back to last known-good cert chain on gateways in eu & ap. Can we re-publish the old secret from vault?
Devon: we have last_good in s3: s3://rotator-backups/eu/20240214-previous-chain.pem. I can push that to k8s as secret.
Sam: before that — let's confirm RBAC: rotator service account in eu-role lacks kms:Decrypt for the new key version. Why did rotation start without that permission?
Kevin: looks like role drift during the cross-region policy migration. The rotator's IAM policy got replaced with the new template missing `kms:Decrypt` on the alias. We'll need a fix and an audit event.
Frank: action list proposal: 
1) Devon: push last_good cert to k8s for prod-gateway in eu & ap (hotfix).
2) Sam/Security: update rotator IAM to include kms:Decrypt for alias/rotator-* keys in eu and ap.
3) Maria: temporarily disable session ticket resume (TLS resumption) on proxies to avoid resume-related failure modes while we stabilize.
4) Kevin: add audit log markers for key unwrap failures and cert promotions (structured fields).
5) Postmortem + vuln triage to prevent role drift during cross-region policy rollouts.
Devon: I'm on (1). Command I will run: 
```
kubectl -n gateway set secret tls gateway-cert --cert=/tmp/previous-chain.pem --key=/tmp/previous-key.pem --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
Devon: doing a staged rollout to 2 pods first, will watch handshake rate.
Maria: (reacts :thumbsup:)
Sam: for (2) propose policy snippet: 
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:DescribeKey"],
  "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/*", "arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:123456789012:key/*"]
}
```
Sam: we'd scope to the rotator key ARNs once we confirm exact ARNs. Add conditional restricting to rotator service principal.
Kevin: for (3) disabling session tickets: update envoy config to set `session_ticket_keys` empty and set `reuse_session_ tickets: false` (apologies for config shorthand). We should do this for a short maintenance window to avoid broad client regressions.
Frank: audit logging — we need structured events emitted when: KMS unwrap fails, rotator publishes incomplete chain, and when proxy rejects handshake for cipher/key-info. Make sure these flow to splunk with host+region tags.
Maria: also add a one-off check: scan other regions for role drift (iam:simulatePrincipalPolicy?) before we re-run rotation elsewhere.
Devon: rolling back in eu; 2 pods patched -> handshake fail rate dropped from 4.8% to 0.9% in 90s.
Kevin: good. Assignments: Devon -> deploy rollback (in progress). Sam -> create IAM patch + PR to infra. Maria -> schedule session-ticket disable and announce maintenance. Frank -> add audit events + dashboard tile. I'll open incident HRT-20240214-01 and ping SRE oncall.
Sam: Q: do we need to re-issue session ticket keys to clients? If we turn resumes off, clients will do full handshake and may cache the new chain once we republish correct cert. We should be fine.
Devon: confirm: after rotator IAM fix we'll re-run rotation in canary with unwrap verification step and new audit event.
Maria: postmortem owners? Sam + Kevin + Devon. We should include timeline, IAM drift root cause, and action to prevent policy template regressions.
Kevin: thanks everyone. continuing in incident channel and will post updates.
devops-bot: Incident created HRT-20240214-01 (severity: high) — links: https://incidents.redwood/2024/HRT-20240214-01
Maria: closing here for now, moving discussion to #incidents/HRT-20240214-01.
